feedback: Written before this candidate has raced; no outcome is stated for it. (1) In iteration 0 the baseline 4 cm array (x = -0.02 to +0.02) at a 5 cm lead gave 1-2 line-loss events per run and every run went off_track at 10-15% progress (outcome table, entityR2B). The line leaves the array on bends, so the controller depends on the array staying over the tape. (2) The baseline oscillation was low (0.07-0.15), so the sensor spacing does not appear to be causing jitter. (3) Integration needed kp raised and kd added to match the wider array and lighter chassis. This is a design choice, not measured evidence. Next race: if line_loss_events is 0 but the robot still leaves the track, the forward offset is the likely limit, so try y = 0.03 m (requested change 1). If steering_oscillation rises above the baseline 0.15 while line losses stay at 0, try a larger sensor pitch or a smaller forward offset. If completion_time is near 3.0 s with completion at 1, try a narrower wheel_track of 0.10 m to turn more readily.
requested_changes: If line_loss_events is 0 but the robot still goes off_track, move the sensors forward to y = 0.03 m (from 0.04) to read the bend earlier. Baseline: a 5 cm lead gave 1-2 losses and off_track on all 60 runs (entityR2B).

If steering_oscillation exceeds about 0.15 while line_loss_events stays 0, widen the pitch to 0.02 m (x from -0.04 to +0.04) to reduce sensitivity per cm. Baseline oscillation was 0.07-0.15, so this only applies if the new geometry raises it.

If completion_time is above about 2.9 s with completion at 1, reduce wheel_track to 0.10 m, keeping the same sensor layout, so the robot turns more readily. Iteration-0 evidence: wheel_track 0.12 and mass 0.8 gave no finishes, so drive response is still unmeasured at the lighter 0.6 kg mass.
